candidate.answerReason: The conditions force the stack R5, B5, R1, B3, R3, B6, R2, B4, R4, or its reverse. Its middle three numbers are 3, 3, and 6.

methods.label: Force the endpoints and work inward
methods.explanation:
Write \(R_k\) for the red card numbered \(k\), and \(B_k\) for the blue card numbered \(k\). With five red cards and four blue cards, alternation forces the color pattern
\[
R,B,R,B,R,B,R,B,R.
\]
The card \(R_5\) can neighbor only \(B_5\), and \(R_4\) can neighbor only \(B_4\). An interior red card needs two distinct blue neighbors, so \(R_5\) and \(R_4\) must occupy the two ends.

Reversing the stack does not change its middle three cards, so start with \(R_5\). The next card must be \(B_5\), whose other red neighbor must be \(R_1\). Thus the first three cards are \(R_5,B_5,R_1\).

At the other end, \(R_4\) must neighbor \(B_4\). The inner red neighbor of \(B_4\) must be \(R_1\) or \(R_2\). Since \(R_1\) already occupies the third position, this neighbor is \(R_2\).

The only remaining red card, \(R_3\), occupies the fifth position. The blue card between \(R_3\) and \(R_2\) must be divisible by both \(3\) and \(2\), so it is \(B_6\). The remaining blue card is \(B_3\). Therefore the stack is forced to be
\[
R_5,B_5,R_1,B_3,R_3,B_6,R_2,B_4,R_4,
\]
or its reverse. Every neighboring pair in this stack satisfies the stated divisibility rule, establishing that the forced arrangement is possible.

The middle three cards are \(B_3,R_3,B_6\), so their sum is \(3+3+6=12\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
